query: Which perturbation and missingness models (MCAR/MAR/MNAR, correlated noise) and magnitude ranges best simulate real EHR errors for testing explanation stability?

response.query: Which perturbation and missingness models (MCAR/MAR/MNAR, correlated noise) and magnitude ranges best simulate real EHR errors for testing explanation stability?
response.answer: MCAR, MAR, and MNAR models, along with correlated noise, best simulate real EHR errors. MCAR has no relation to missingness, MAR relates to missingness and observed data, MNAR depends on unobserved data. Magnitude ranges of 1-10% simulate realistic errors.

In this paper, we explore alternative way of leveraging Large Language Model (LLM) generated feedback to address the inherent limitation of using human-labeled data. Recent research in federated large language models (LLMs) has primarily focused on enabling clients to fine-tune their locally deployed homogeneous LLMs collaboratively or on transferring knowledge from server-based LLMs to small language models (SLMs) at downstream clients. Our analysis demonstrates that this task is highly challenging, with large language models (LLMs) yielding unsatisfactory performance.
